rounds.text: Nakoda Group of Industries Ltd carries severe valuation and fundamental risks that are unsupported by the underlying evidence. The stock trades at an inflated P/E ratio of 42.6x to 43.06x, which sits well above the sector benchmark of 30.8x [E1, E6]. This rich multiple is completely decoupled from its historical and projected fundamentals, underscored by a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 12 per share leading to a staggering margin of safety of -215.5% [E41, E42]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that today's price of Rs 37.5 demands an aggressive 18.6% earnings growth, vastly eclipsing the base-case assumption of 3.0% [E2, E43]. Compounded sales growth paints a stagnant picture with a 3-year contraction of -7% and a lackluster 1% over the trailing twelve months, while long-term top-line expansion crawls at just 7% over 5 years [E14, E15, E16]. Profitability metrics are similarly underwhelming, highlighted by a 3-year median return on equity of -6% and a 10-year median ROE of just 1% [E23, E25]. Additionally, promoter confidence appears to be waning as insider holdings have dropped by 7.91 percentage points from 65.20% in September 2023 to 57.29% by June 2026 [E38]. Conceded: [E19, E22, E27].

Conceded: [E1, E6, E41, E42, E43, E14, E15, E16, E23, E25, E38]. While the bear focuses heavily on backward-looking metrics and rigid DCF models, it ignores the explosive, live inflection occurring in the business today [E19, E27]. Compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months has surged by a remarkable 156%, proving that current earnings power is vastly outpacing historical medians [E19]. Furthermore, operating margins have expanded dramatically by 10 percentage points to 11% in the TTM compared to three years prior [E27]. The company is converting this profit into cold cash exceptionally well, registering a cash conversion ratio of 2.83x with operating cash flow reaching Rs 4.25 Cr and free cash flow hitting Rs 2.09 Cr [E31, E32, E33]. Finally, market participants are recognizing this acceleration, pushing the stock with a stellar 12-month price return of 28.6% and a relative-strength rating of 92 against the Nifty 500 [E47, E48].

Conceded: [E19, E27]. While the bull points to a 156% surge in TTM profit growth and a 10 percentage point margin expansion, these headline figures mask a broader, chronic stagnation in top-line expansion, evidenced by a negative 3-year sales growth of -7% and a paltry 1% TTM sales growth [E15, E16, E19, E27]. Conceded: [E31, E32, E33]. Despite healthy recent operating and free cash flows, the company's historical profitability remains deeply depressed, reflected in a 10-year median ROE of 1% and a 3-year median ROE of -6%, alongside returns on capital that persistently lag sector benchmarks [E8, E10, E23, E25]. Furthermore, the bull's reliance on a 28.6% 12-month return and a relative-strength rating of 92 ignores the extreme volatility and historical fragility of the equity, which carries an annualized volatility of 60.3% and a catastrophic worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -92.8% [E47, E48, E49, E50]. Finally, insiders are voting with their feet rather than rewarding this operational inflection, as promoter holding has steadily eroded from 65.20% in September 2023 to 57.29% by June 2026 [E38].
